texts.facts: 1 BRIEF FACTS: 2. Briefly stated, it was the case of the complainant/FSO that samples of 'Mixed Fruit Jam' in sealed container were lifted by the Food Safety Officer from M/s. The Leela Palace (A unit of M/s. Leela Venture Ltd.), Diplomatic Enclave, New Delhi110023 for analysis under FSS Act on 29.05.2017, where the said food articles were found stored for serving or selling to the customers for human consumption. The samples consisting of four sealed jars of 'Mixed Fruit Jam', each Jar containing 1 Kg taken as such in original condition bearing identical label declaration. It was the case of the complainant/FSO that samples were divided into four equal parts by converting one sealed jar 'Mixed Fruit Jam' as one counter part of the sample and one counter part of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst for examination. It appears that the no request was made by Food Business Operator to send 4th part of the sample for analysis from NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of the Food Safety & Standars Rules, 2011 (for short 'FSSR'), and accordingly the counter parts of the samples in sealed packet as well as 4th counter part in separate packet were deposited with the designated officer on 30.05.2017. The Food Analyst vide his report dated 07.06.2017 found that percentage of ingredients used i.e. mix fruits was not declared in the labels although the label emphasized through pictures, and therefore, the sample was found to be misbranded for violation of regulation 2.2.2.2 (f) (i) of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling), 2011; and on the basis of said report, a complaint was filed before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM). 3. Notice was issued to the appellants and after hearing, the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order dated 25.02.2022. It is pertinent to mention here that in the initial complaint seven accused persons were arraigned for inquiry/trial viz. respondent No.1 Vinod Saini of M/s. The Leela Palace; respondent No.2 M/s. The Leela Palace itself and respondent No.3 Sandeep Sudhan of M/s. Kanhiya Lal Kishori Lal, which firm was arraigned as respondent No.4. Further, the respondent No.5 Archit Aggarwal and respondent No.6 Suresh Chander Sharma were arraigned as Directors for accused No.7 company M/s. Vidya Sagar Food Pvt. Ltd. 4. The record brings out that the said order was assailed in an appeal earlier in FSAT No. 16/2018 whereby the learned Predecessor of this Court Ms. Poonam A. Bamba, the then Ld. District & Sessions Judge, New Delhi (as her Ladyship was then) vide judgment dated 01.04.2019 allowed the Mr. Archit Aggarwal vs Shri Hukum Singh on 12 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192191821/ 2 joint appeal filed by the appellant Nos. 3 and 4 besides appellant Nos. 5 and 6. It would be expedient to refer to the relevant paragraphs whereby the appeal was considered and remanded back to the Ld. Adjudicating Officer to hear the parties and record his specific findings on the contentions raised by the "the appellant, which go as under: " 8.3.1 It is seen that the Ld.ADM found the manufacturer as well as supplier guilty of the aforesaid violations. 9.0 Another error which is noted in the impugned order, is that while concluding the violations, Ld.ADM has recorded the violations as 26(2)(ii), 23(1) & 27(3)(c) read with Section 3(1) (zf)(c)(i) of FSS Act and Regulation 2.2.2.3 and 2.2.2.10 of FSS(P&L) Regulations. Whereas, the appellants have been found guilty of violation of regulation 2.2.2.2(f)(i) of the said Regulation and not Regulation 2.2.2.3 and 2.2.2.10. 9.1 In view of the above facts and circumstances, the matter needs to be remanded back to Ld. ADM for recording specific findings w.r.t. liability of the manufacturing company and also for necessary correction w.r.t. regulation, for violation of which, the appellants have been penalised. 10.0 The appellants have also contended that Delhi Food Laboratory in which the sample was analyzed and issued analytical report, is not legally competent lab to analyze the samples of food under FSS Act as per Section 43 of FSS Act; as the same is neither NABL Accredited nor notified in the Official Gazette as per provisions Section 3(1)(p) FSS Act. It is also contended that no penalty should have been imposed on the appellants as Section 32 FSS Act mandates that prosecution should not be initiated for minor defects. Hence, relief is claimed to setaside the impugned order dated 25.02.2022. 8. Notice of the present appeal was issued to the respondent and vide order dated 29.04.2022 the operation of the impugned order was stayed subject to furnishing of Demand Draft/FDR by the appellants to the extent of 50% of the amount of find imposed by the Ld. Adjudicating Officer (ADM), which has been complied with. The earlier order was modified on 28.10.2022 clarifying that demand draft in the sum of Rs. 80,000/ has been placed on the record by the appellants. The respondent has opposed the appeal and has supported the legality of the impugned order.
